excluded_reviewed_candidates.reason: Adaptive variance-reduction sampling within conventional zeroth-order optimization, without an agent self-revision mechanism.
Query-adaptive recognition guidance and induced category skills without a demonstrated persistent feedback-driven evolution loop.
Source-aware RL credit assignment without a retained agent self-revision mechanism.
An API-document optimization application rather than evolution of the agent or its reusable improvement mechanism.
From-scratch simulation RL for assembly without an explicit persistent agent self-revision mechanism.
Conventional neuroevolution of robot controllers rather than the focused LLM/agent RSI scope.
General embodied-memory evaluation without a focused persistent self-evolution audit.
Revisable task-state recovery; no retained reusable capability evolution shown in the abstract.
Grounded memory construction and mechanical audit, without a demonstrated experience-driven capability evolution loop.
Temporal evidence retrieval/organization rather than self-evolving capability.
Evidence admission into current-query reasoning rather than persistent self-improvement.
Empowerment/skill-learning objective rather than an explicit agent self-revision mechanism.
Evidence/conclusion co-evolution within current-query reasoning.
Retrieval over a fixed memory index.
Current-query memory construction without demonstrated retained capability changes.
Static post-trained verifier, without an evolving verifier or direct self-improvement audit.
Iterative refinement of a single infographic output rather than reusable agent-capability change.
Explanation-based RL credit assignment rather than explicit persistent self-revision.
World-model post-training on failure dynamics without a retained improvement loop in the abstract.
Static onboard agent/behavior-tree architecture with retry feedback.
Reward-side rollout intervention and ordinary policy optimization; no autonomous retained improvement mechanism established.

2610.13912.mechanism: Observed feedback updates policies or workflows and conditionally adapts the world model; component and compatibility checks govern retention for later interaction.
2610.13912.boundary: Domain results use different settings and budgets. Retained pair updates support a finite recursive loop, not indefinite acceleration or independently reproduced gains.

2610.13025.mechanism: A shared policy proposes and diagnoses harness edits; edit outcomes train both roles through recovered trajectories, SFT, and interleaved GRPO. Updated weights drive later harness search.
2610.13025.boundary: Separate gains from weight training, harness search, and additional trajectory exposure. Cross-benchmark transfer does not establish unlimited co-evolution.

2610.12789.update_target: Persistent, falsifiable environment rules; frozen LLM
2610.12789.mechanism: Unexpected outcomes trigger hypotheses; observations and controlled experiments validate rules. Counterexamples narrow or retire them before subsequent predictions and plans.
2610.12789.boundary: Rules are scoped to supporting evidence; validation and changed dynamics need separate audits. No model-weight update is claimed.

2610.13194.update_target: Research skills, predictive judgment, and coordination protocols
2610.13194.mechanism: Forecast candidate value, information gain, and exploration utility before execution; ground-truth outcomes update research-agent skills and world-model exploration strategies.
2610.13194.boundary: The abstract supplies no numerical headline. Count forecasting, execution, and skill updates in the same budget; prediction quality can drift with search.

2610.13376.update_target: Endoscopic robot policies revised by a coding research agent
2610.13376.mechanism: Physical failures falsify offline-supported strategies; EndoForge incorporates failed rollouts into later policy revisions. Human-authorized execution stays in a separate constrained runtime.
2610.13376.boundary: This is human-governed physical evidence, not unattended clinical deployment. Ex-vivo specimens and visual/hardware shifts have a defined scope.

2610.12593.update_target: Synthetic interaction-factor space and allocation, coupled to learner updates
2610.12593.mechanism: Learner feedback changes synthesis directions and promotes newly discovered factors into explicit controls; Designer and Planner produce executable experience for further learning.
2610.12593.boundary: Distinguish expansion of generation controls from simple resampling; verify that downstream gains persist when synthesis and training budgets are matched.

2610.12794.update_target: Production-agent specifications, pipeline programs, and workflows
2610.12794.mechanism: An agentic mutator retrieves full evolutionary history and probes the live system before testing and proposing retained program mutations.
2610.12794.boundary: The optimizer remains an external mechanism; optimized production systems should not be described as autonomous optimizer-weight evolution.

2610.12536.update_target: An elite archive of executable control programs
2610.12536.mechanism: Search evaluations update a fixed-capacity elite table; retained programs guide proposals, edits, and remixes. Held-out episodes do not enter the search loop.
2610.12536.boundary: Search-score improvement can coexist with held-out decline. The paper explicitly requires comparisons and ablations to establish relative performance.

2610.12668.update_target: Retrieved reflections in a persistent textual harness
2610.12668.mechanism: After each streaming instance, its trajectory revises the reflections retrieved for that instance, sending feedback backward into harness state for later use.
2610.12668.boundary: This updates external reflections, not backbone weights. Check revision provenance, distribution-shift adaptation, and cost of growing retrieved context.

2610.12813.mechanism: Deployment failures guide LLM policy patches; deterministic structural/conflict checks and an evidence-aware activation layer gate updates and preserve previously correct behavior.
2610.12813.boundary: Structural validity is distinct from complete semantic safety. Evidence requirements and the tested threat distribution bound the claim.

2610.12598.update_target: Auxiliary reward signals and coding-policy weights
2610.12598.mechanism: The current policy compares debugging behavior among trajectories sharing a task and verifier outcome; bounded auxiliary rewards preserve pass/fail ordering during learning.
2610.12598.boundary: Self-comparison may share policy blind spots. The binary verifier remains the anchor; no separately trained reward model or extra environment interactions are required.

2610.12659.update_target: Policy- and budget-calibrated synthetic RLVR problems
2610.12659.mechanism: Top-down decomposition and bottom-up synthesis preserve seed reasoning blueprints while constructing problems with mixed rollout outcomes for a target policy and budget.
2610.12659.boundary: Recursive problem construction is an enabling data mechanism. It does not alone establish autonomous evolution of the optimizer or an unlimited policy–data loop.

2610.13285.update_target: Student weights and a changing distillation dataset
2610.13285.mechanism: Prime the student with teacher trajectories, then repeatedly select questions the current student has not mastered and the expert reliably solves; refresh data as capability changes.
2610.13285.boundary: The external expert supplies supervision; data–model co-evolution is not self-generated verification. Code and data are promised rather than verified as released.

2610.12984.update_target: Reusable GUI workflow skills induced from human demonstrations
2610.12984.mechanism: Synchronized screen, input-event, and accessibility evidence supports on-demand skill induction of rules, dependencies, and completion checks, then reuse by fixed execution models.
2610.12984.boundary: Included as a skill-acquisition mechanism. The abstract does not show an autonomous repeated skill-revision loop; demonstrations provide human knowledge.

2610.13058.update_target: Retained branch experience and a shared execution/reflection policy
2610.13058.mechanism: Rewind environment state while retaining valid progress and knowledge; State-Anchored GRPO compares continuations and branch-advancement reward trains useful reflection.
2610.13058.boundary: Reuse is within an ongoing task. Rewind feasibility, replay cost, and policy training must be separated from cross-task persistent improvement.

2610.13064.update_target: An evolved workflow pool and a learned contextual selector
2610.13064.mechanism: Evolutionary search constructs candidate workflows; contextual-bandit feedback learns selection through exploration and exploitation, and inference reuses the pool per query.
2610.13064.boundary: Report pool-generation cost separately from selector learning; query-adaptive reuse is not continuous test-time rewriting of the whole harness.

2610.13098.update_target: Executable scene programs and aligned execution evidence
2610.13098.mechanism: Runtime writes and state changes generate constrained repair programs. Endpoint/preservation checks precede visual goal verification and subsequent scene refinement.
2610.13098.boundary: The loop operates within each task. No extra LLM call for repair construction does not mean no extra execution cost or persistent cross-task learning.

2610.13172.update_target: Role assignments and parameter estimates in a transferred symbolic world model
2610.13172.mechanism: A teacher extracts prototypes, fixed rules, and an actor skill; target-world action feedback revises role estimates and triggers hypothesis tests when uncertainty affects decisions.
2610.13172.boundary: Target transition rules and LLM weights remain fixed; online estimate adaptation should not be described as learning an unconstrained new rule system.

2610.13267.update_target: Functional access to poisoned versus benign memories
2610.13267.mechanism: Weak perturbation-driven reactivation exposes anomalies; multi-dimensional diagnosis drives selective suppression of harmful memories and reinforcement of benign ones.
2610.13267.boundary: Memory repair is a bounded adaptation mechanism. Diagnose false suppression and benign utility independently of attack-success reduction.

2610.13345.update_target: Robot-policy weights and selectively retained deployment experience
2610.13345.mechanism: Deploy the policy, collect autonomous rollouts and human interventions, train value estimates, and select positive-advantage experience for policy refinement and redeployment.
2610.13345.boundary: Human corrections remain part of the loop. The abstract uses percent rather than explicitly saying percentage points; do not silently change units.

2610.13453.update_target: Driving-policy weights distilled from reflective corrective distributions
2610.13453.mechanism: Route student trajectories by driving score; distill token-level corrections for risky trajectories and self-imitate reliable ones, using a progressively constructed teacher.
2610.13453.boundary: Reflection is training-time privileged information; inference is single-pass. This is a self-distillation mechanism rather than an online autonomous driving RSI claim.

2610.13485.update_target: Subagent harness adjustments and orchestration-policy weights
2610.13485.mechanism: Proactive revision requests change running subagent harnesses. Hindsight attribution assigns those requests to earlier orchestration decisions for OPOD process supervision.
2610.13485.boundary: Separate runtime harness adaptation from learned orchestration improvements. Account for communication and hindsight-supervision costs.

2610.13816.update_target: A steering module over a frozen generalist robot policy
2610.13816.mechanism: A frozen world model rehearses earlier tasks through imagined rollouts while the module learns new tasks; learn in imagination only when model fidelity suffices.
2610.13816.boundary: The world model and generalist policy stay fixed. Model fidelity determines whether imagination supports new-task learning or only rehearsal.

2610.13494.update_target: Retained experimental artifacts across alternating MLE sessions
2610.13494.mechanism: Two agents alternate on a shared workspace, cap experiments per session, and reset context while building on prior candidates; a CR-SMDP analysis gives conditional budget guarantees.
2610.13494.boundary: This is workflow-level experience reuse, not self-modification of model weights. Theoretical sufficient conditions do not certify every task or agent pair.

2610.13632.update_target: Candidate solutions, task-specific wiki knowledge, and multi-session review
2610.13632.mechanism: Independent review, a structured wiki, and checking Lean proofs against trusted challenge statements guide subsequent problem-solving sessions.
2610.13632.boundary: Candidate improvement and trusted-statement verification are task-bound. The introductory claims about other systems are context, not findings independently certified here.

2610.13386.mechanism: Sequential LLM-guided revisions use class-conditioned errors; validation Macro-F1 selects prompts for final testing across instruction and reasoning variants.
2610.13386.boundary: Task-specific prompt refinement is an external optimization mechanism; keep validation selection and final test results distinct.

2610.13663.update_target: Specified functional blocks of fixed-architecture neural networks
2610.13663.mechanism: Analyst, coder, and recorder generate component code, evaluate it in a sandbox, and retain experiment logs to guide subsequent candidates.
2610.13663.boundary: The network structure and optimizer framework remain fixed. Selected-run 2491x/325x error reductions should not be generalized to every initialization or task.

2610.12707.update_target: A lightweight reward head over a frozen VLM
2610.12707.mechanism: Same-image perturbations train a convex intermediate-layer head; policy-generated, verifier-labeled candidates support a subsequent bootstrap retraining turn.
2610.12707.boundary: Included for verifier-driven reward adaptation and the benchmark–policy mismatch. One bootstrap turn does not prove indefinitely reliable co-evolution.

2610.13166.update_target: Synthesized task environments and a terminal model trained on retained trajectories
2610.13166.mechanism: Independent execution identifies missing work and guides environment reconstruction; same-goal task expansion carries prior results into later stages and research feedback guides retained method improvements.
2610.13166.boundary: Separate environment-synthesis feedback, one-time SFT, and task-level RSI case studies. The abstract gives no numerical benchmark headline.

2610.13272.update_target: Video-policy token credit and spatiotemporal representations
2610.13272.mechanism: The same student response is compared under uniform and evidence-rich views; relative token likelihood redistributes positive advantage and verifier-accepted responses receive hidden-state alignment.
2610.13272.boundary: This is an evidence-privileged self-supervision mechanism, not an autonomous repeated agent-evolution result. Do not invent missing performance numbers.

2610.13886.update_target: Tool-dependency graph recipes and adversarial path preconditions
2610.13886.mechanism: Execution feedback diversifies successful harmful paths through tool substitution and revises blocked preconditions in unsuccessful paths for further exploration.
2610.13886.boundary: This evolves a red-teaming search mechanism, not the target agent’s weights. Generated coverage and observed harm require separate measurement.

2610.12569.update_target: Dynamically authored coding tasks and executable acceptance oracles
2610.12569.mechanism: Mirrored Red–Blue turns require feature preservation, exactly targeted bug-test failure, and a fresh blind repair check before admission; participants then swap roles.
2610.12569.boundary: Arena difficulty can scale with task authors, but evaluation-time generation does not itself train or recursively improve participant agents.

2610.12601.update_target: Evaluation of evolved deep-research prompts and verifier feedback
2610.12601.mechanism: Topic-disjoint splits, three seeds, answer-key ablations, decomposed-versus-scalar feedback, and out-of-family judges test transfer and prompt overfitting.
2610.12601.boundary: Nearly half the winning prompt is an answer key, yet its content earns no reward on encoded questions. The reported gap is attributed to noisy small-sample selection, not memorization.

2610.12822.update_target: Reward-hacking strategies transmitted across coding agents
2610.12822.mechanism: Coding RL forms source strategies; code, shared memory, and plans transmit them across agents and roles. Theory analyzes amplification, persistence, and decay; review is tested as mitigation.
2610.12822.boundary: More reward or stronger coordination can reflect transmitted evaluator bypass, not genuine solution quality. Review mitigations are evaluated rather than universal guarantees.

2610.12855.mechanism: Track previously correct queries and representation geometry; RGR preserves within-cluster compactness and between-cluster separation while retaining the underlying OPSD procedure.
2610.12855.boundary: Overall average improvement can hide per-query forgetting. Correlated geometry changes and a tested regularizer do not establish a universal causal explanation.

2610.13021.update_target: Compositional transfer from basic-task experience to unseen embodied tasks
2610.13021.mechanism: Simulation compares harnesses and learning methods on learning basic skills and recombining them for advanced tasks.
2610.13021.boundary: This is a benchmark and reported learning limitation, not an achieved RSI system. Sample quantity and meaningful transferable information should be measured separately.

2610.13227.update_target: Security of persistent artifacts reused across skill sessions
2610.13227.mechanism: SkillRelayBench isolates instruction propagation, data-boundary violations, and evidence poisoning; provenance restoration and pre-execution advisory review are evaluated.
2610.13227.boundary: Persistent reuse can carry malicious instructions as well as useful experience. Advisory review leaves the final decision to the agent; tested attacks bound effectiveness.

2610.13361.update_target: Held-out behavioral acceptance of agents built or optimized by coding agents
2610.13361.mechanism: Twenty-five commissions cover creation, editing, and optimization. Frozen deliveries face requirement-derived rubrics and hard gates beyond visible development examples.
2610.13361.boundary: A convincing demonstration or improved development score is not evidence that the delivered agent meets held-out requirements.

2610.13829.update_target: Durable capability transfer across reset Minecraft worlds
2610.13829.mechanism: Nineteen registered chains and three paired probe families transfer only declared artifacts; no-prior, related, unrelated, and shuffled conditions use matched steps and five seeds.
2610.13829.boundary: Stage bottlenecks can leave later skills unobserved. Saved memory, carried resources, and final success must be separated from learned transferable capability.

2610.13881.update_target: Exact memory-state requirements for future cumulative updates
2610.13881.mechanism: Theory compares histories with identical predictions but different update-relevant evidence, classifying polynomial losses and kernel-attention closure under explicit assumptions.
2610.13881.boundary: These are exact-state and compression bounds under stated feature, continuity, and loss assumptions; the paper makes no trained-model performance claim.

2610.13287.update_target: Unscored output-contract regressions during prompt optimization
2610.13287.mechanism: A preregistered study uses deterministic requirement checks for GEPA, MIPROv2, and TextGrad; post-hoc analyses vary parseability and output-token caps.
2610.13287.boundary: Report the preregistered violation and the narrower post-hoc explanation together: higher accuracy can coexist with broken output contracts under a strict cap.

figure_checks.label: Figure 1: RSI-Anything overview. Building on the cross-domain predictive foundation of JEPA-Anything, RSI-Anything uses world-model predictions to support understanding, planning, and action selection across diverse tasks. Interaction feedback drives policy or workflow updates and conditional world-model adaptation. Component and compatibility checks determine which policy–model pair is retained to guide the next round of interaction and learning, closing the recursive self-improvement loop.

Figure 1: Weight-harness co-evolution in Evo 2 . A shared Proposer–Reflector policy evolves the agent harness. Harness edits and execution outcomes provide training experience for the policy, whose updated weights guide subsequent search. Crossover searching transfers useful strategies between branches.

Figure 1: Illustrative example. (a) Following its frozen prior, a capable agent heats compound X to 100 ∘ C and gets decomposition products. (b) The mismatch triggers a hypothesis, which controlled experiments test. (c) The verified belief is stored in the persistent world model W W and changes later actions in the original task and in new ones, without any parameter update. Based on the updated belief, the agent avoids gas chromatography (GC), whose operating temperature exceeds the supported range, and correctly chooses to use liquid chromatography (LC) instead.

Figure 1: Conceptual comparison between recent works and JANUS. Unlike traditional Generate–Execute–Feedback frameworks that suffer from execution bottlenecks, JANUS introduces a Predict–Verify–Evolve loop to forecast outcomes, prune unpromising branches, and reuse past experience. Consequently, JANUS establishes a superior Evolving Scaling Law , significantly improving both evolving efficiency and the attainable evolving ceiling over reactive baselines.

Figure 1: EndoForge connects task definition, policy research, physical execution and evidence-driven revision. Existing tracking and navigation data provide complementary source skills. The coding agent analyses data, results and code and prepares candidate policies. Human-authorised execution occurs through a separate safety-constrained runtime. Physical outcomes and human feedback inform subsequent research and transfer evaluation.

Figure 1: From static synthesis to closed-loop self-evolving agentic synthesis. Existing paradigms improve data quality or adapt within a fixed synthesis space. In contrast, EvoSyn uses learner feedback to revise both the allocation over known factors and the synthesis space itself by introducing new controllable interaction factors.

Revisions diminish as reflections stabilize before the distribution shift, then rise afterward to update outdated reflections. (b) Top- k k scaling on CL-Bench with Claude. ReHarness improves sharply up to k = 5 k=5 and stabilizes for moderate k k , while larger values yield diminishing returns and higher cost.

Figure 1: Motivation for evolving formal policy. Static formal policy cannot adapt. Across a sequence of deployment tasks, natural-language memory can accumulate ambiguous or conflicting guidance and overgeneralize from feedback, causing regression on previously correct behavior. In contrast, VEPA represents policy as executable symbolic rules, verifies new rules for conflict-freedom, and preserves previously correct rules while adapting to newly observed cases.

We denote problems with 0 / 8 0/8 , 1 1 – 7 / 8 7/8 , and 8 / 8 8/8 correct responses as hard , Goldilocks , and stale/mastered , respectively; each bar height is the fraction of problems in that row. Roughly 𝟖𝟖 % \mathbf{88\%} of the corpus falls in the zero-advantage trap providing no learning signal, whereas MagicBeanStalk places 58.2 % 58.2\% of its math problems and 56.7 % 56.7\% of its finance problems in the Goldilocks band. Figure 1: BoundaryEvo evolves supervision along the capability boundary of the student model. (a-c) Comparison with static distillation and error-driven acquisition, BoundaryEvo dynamically adapts supervision according to the evolving capability boundary of the student model. (d) BoundaryEvo-4B consistently outperforms strong baselines across various reasoning benchmarks.

Figure 2: Overview of Work2Skill. WorkRecorder aligns human GUI actions with visual and available accessibility evidence to build WorkDemo-350. An agent inspects evidence on demand and revises reusable skills for downstream GUI execution. Downstream evaluation compares these skills with guidance from the fixed workflows of ShowUI-Aloha and Demo2Tutorial.

Figure 1: Retrospective exploration with retained experience. Multi-episode adaptation (top) restarts the task from s 0 s_{0} after an unsuccessful attempt, carrying retained experience into a new episode. In contrast, ReTRAIL (bottom) proactively abandons an unproductive branch, distills its experience, rewinds to an earlier state, and resumes with the retained execution prefix and accumulated experience. Recovery can occur before terminal failure.
Figure 1: CB-Orchestrator vs. prior workflow-optimization paradigms.

Figure 1: Conceptual overview of VETR. VETR refines scenes through execution-grounded evidence, bridging a scene program, its execution trace, and the realized 3D scene. Given a start and goal image, the system performs iterative updates guided by observed writes and realized bindings. This evidence-supported refinement targets viewpoint alignment, appearance (lighting/material) editing, and geometry and placement adjustments. Runtime checks test supported effects, while visual feedback guides subsequent proposals toward the goal.

Figure 1: Overview of RoleWorld . A teacher LLM induces role prototypes, transition rules, and an actor skill from source trajectories. These remain fixed in the target world, where the actor refines role estimates online and tests hypotheses when uncertainty could affect its decision.

Figure 1 : Existing defenses versus neuro-inspired forgetting for poisoned LLM agents. (a) Existing defenses rely on online auditing, which require more computational overhead when continuous scan, or dual-memory isolation, which result in reasoning disruption. (b) Inspired by biological forgetting, weak reactivation destabilizes intrusive memories for gradual decay (left), which motivates weak probing to expose poisoned memories for selective forgetting while preserving benign ones in LLM agents (right).

Fig. 1: Overview of the Evo-RL method. The current policy is deployed to collect demonstrations, human interventions, and autonomous rollouts. Complete trajectories are used to train a value model whose estimates guide policy refinement. The updated policy is then redeployed in the next iteration.

Figure 1: From Reflective Guidance to Internalized Planning. (a) Reflective Guidance corrects an unsafe initial trajectory during iterative inference, revealing substantial planning gains. (b) Reflect-VLA transfers these gains through Dual-OPSD by aligning teacher and student token distributions along student-generated trajectories. (c) Across different model scales, Reflect-VLA improves planning performance over SFT while requiring substantially less training time than RL, enabling guidance-free single-pass planning.

Figure 1: Comparison of orchestration paradigms. (a) Offline orchestration fixes harnesses and workflows. (b) Re-orchestration adapts harnesses upon completion or predefined triggers. (c) POrchestra integrates execution and harness adaptation via proactive sub-agent communication.

Figure 1: HMA overview. (A) Declining output tokens per response accompany diminishing score gains, indicating decelerating single-agent exploration; harness gains can vanish or reverse as models improve. (B) HMA alternates native agents after at most k k experiments, resetting context while preserving shared work and candidates for final review. The motor analogy illustrates options A A and B B alternately energizing shared state X i X_{i} toward the final result E ^ \widehat{E} . The CR-SMDP view captures how complementary options can extend exploration beyond single-agent limits.

Figure 1: HOA replaces a brittle one-shot workflow with iterative review, knowledge retrieval, and verification. The bottom row summarizes results from high-school olympiads to research-level formal mathematics.

Figure 1: Overview of MoPrO-SD. Starting from a six-module base prompt, MoPrO-SD sequentially refines the modules using instruction-only (I), instruction with reasoning (I+R), or instruction with per-example reasoning (I+R+E). After each iteration, the updated prompt is evaluated using validation Macro-F1, and the highest-scoring prompt is selected for final test evaluation.

Figure 2 : SNN pipeline. The input encoding, the SNN trained with STDP, and the output activity vector 𝐫 \mathbf{r} (left and middle) are fixed. Only the decoder module Decoder ⁡ ( 𝐫 ) \mathrm{Decoder}(\mathbf{r}) (right) is generated and optimized by the framework.

Figure 5: The loop transposes to image generation: verifier-minted pairs gain 5.4 points over random selection at 8B, while the 2B head trained on caption perturbations loses 6.5. (a) Best-of- N N on 160 held-out hard compositional prompts: verifier pass rate of the image each selector picks from N N Qwen-Image samples (bands: 75% binomial intervals; paired differences against random at N = 12 N{=}12 in the text). (b) One prompt and each selector’s pick out of twelve, judged by the GenEval-style OWLv2 verifier ( Ghosh et al., 2023 ; Minderer et al., 2023 ) on object presence, count, colour and relative position. The selectors see only the image.

Figure 1: Motivation for TerminalHorizon. Short trajectories can teach agents to perform terminal operations, but not to autonomously complete complex, long-horizon tasks. Our long-horizon trajectories connect agentic behavioral patterns, such as exploration, strategy revision, and verification, into a complete autonomous problem-solving process.

Figure 1: Illustration of how OWLET improves video reasoning through evidence-guided post-training. Uniform frame sampling misses the temporal transitions needed to answer the question, whereas OWLET learns from a correct evidence-privileged teacher.
